text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- High Court decides former government delegate for Basque country Julen Elgorriaga to remain in prison for fear he will flee.
- Basque Nationalist Party (PNV) will only approve budget if renegotiation of Basque country's fiscal agreement with central government advances.
- Government has been working for three months on plan for regulating television.
EL MUNDO
- Italy criticises Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and French President Jacques Chirac and denounces "plot" against lira.

- Deputy Prime Minister Francisco Alvarez Cascos says his accusation that former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez ran a 1980s death squad campaign against Basque separatists reflects "the doctrine of the Popular Party (PP)".
- Government returns wig to former communist leader Santiago Carrillo, who wore it when he was arrested 20 years ago.
DIARIO 16
- Madrid mayor Jose Maria Alvarez del Manzano vehemently denies he allowed destruction of city's arab wall.
- Alfonso Guerra, vice secretary-general of Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE), calls Cascos "contemptible" for accusing Gonzalez of creating Anti-terrorist Liberation Groups (GAL).
- Former spy Colonel Juan Alberto Perote tells Diario 16 in an open letter that during a search of his cell no originals or photocopies of military intelligence papers were found.
ABC
- King Juan Carlos says a country is only worth as much as its education system.
CINCO DIAS
- Government to change telephone numbers from February.
- Banco Bilbao Vizcaya invests 44.5 billion pesetas to control Argentina's third-largest private bank, Banco Frances del Rio de la Plata.
- Electricity group Endesa scraps seniority wage bonus and replaces it with productivity-linked perks.
EXPANSION
- Juan Miguel Villar Mir wants to become new king of fertilizers by launching public share offer for Sefanitro through Fertiberia.
- Treasury lowers three- and 10-year bond rates to historical lows.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Government dismantles Socialists' energy plan.
- Firms which hold motorway licences could sell toll rights, according to Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado.
- Telepizza, on the verge of launching on stock exchange, is worth between 23 and 27 billion pesetas.
- British opposition leader Tony Blair commits to signing social chapter of Maastricht treaty in 1997 if elected.
